=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1188-1189 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `classify_preflight_failure` re-scans the full appended log after rerender, so an earlier failure signature can be matched instead of the post-rerender failure.
  WHY: `PRE_FLIGHT_APPEND_LOG="true"` causes both attempts to accumulate in `PRE_FLIGHT_LOG_FILE`, and the classifier’s `grep`-based search can pick the first matching pattern; reviewers disagreed only on framing, not on the underlying bug.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1150-1158 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The render-recovery gate checks `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` before calling `classify_preflight_failure`, creating a redundant classification path that can block recovery if the class marker is stale or inconsistent.
  WHY: Reviewers identified the same root concern that recovery depends on a manually maintained coarse class instead of the log-based classifier; one reviewer disputed that this path can actually go stale, so the severity is kept at the highest reported level with that disagreement noted.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:31-37,82-87,188-244,344-381,486-535,633-691 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The render-recovery tests stub `classify_preflight_failure` instead of exercising the production classifier.
  WHY: This leaves the real `grep`-based classification logic untested, so regressions such as log-accumulation misclassification would not be caught by these scenarios.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1189-1194 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `classify_preflight_failure` is called after rerender while scanning the entire accumulated `PRE_FLIGHT_LOG_FILE`, which can misclassify a second failure if the same pattern appeared in the original attempt.
  WHY: Because `PRE_FLIGHT_APPEND_LOG="true"` keeps both attempts in one file, `grep -Fq` can match the first occurrence and record the wrong `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_REASON`.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1150-1158 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The recovery flow uses both `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` and `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_KIND`, which can disagree and make recovery behavior inconsistent.
  WHY: The gate can skip recovery even when the log-based classifier would say the failure is lint, or proceed when the two mechanisms diverge.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:all test functions with embedded Bash scripts | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The tests stub `classify_preflight_failure` instead of validating the real classification logic.
  WHY: Bugs in the production classifier, including pattern mistakes or log-scanning errors, would not be caught because the stub always returns fixed values.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1148-1158 and 1189 (approximate line numbers in current version) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `classify_preflight_failure` scans the entire accumulated `PRE_FLIGHT_LOG_FILE` when `PRE_FLIGHT_APPEND_LOG="true"`.
  WHY: During rerun recovery, the log contains both the initial failure and the retry, so `grep` can match the first failure signature and misclassify the second one.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1150-1153 (approximate) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` check can block recovery even if `classify_preflight_failure` would identify a fixable lint error.
  WHY: If a new preflight failure path forgets to set `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS="lint"`, the recovery logic is skipped even when the log-based classifier would have marked it recoverable.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1195-1757 (within `run_preflight_checks`) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` is initialized to `"none"` but many failure paths do not update it.
  WHY: Any failure path that leaves the class unset will be treated as non-recoverable by the render-recovery gate, causing valid recovery opportunities to be missed.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:Multiple locations (lines 31-117, 188-302, 344-439, 486-593, 633-749) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The tests use a stubbed/simplified version of `classify_preflight_failure` instead of the production logic.
  WHY: The stub bypasses the real `grep`-based classifier, so the tests do not catch regressions in log parsing or misclassification behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1182-1189 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When render recovery reruns preflight with log appending enabled, `classify_preflight_failure` scans the entire log history and can report the original failure instead of the rerun failure.
  WHY: The second attempt is appended to the same log file, and the classifier uses `grep -Fq`, so the first matching signature in the file can determine the recorded failure reason.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1150-1158 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The recovery flow checks both `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` and `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_KIND`, which can get out of sync and block valid render recovery.
  WHY: If the coarse class says non-lint while the classifier would say lint, recovery is skipped; if they disagree the flow becomes inconsistent.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1199-1201, and various failure handlers | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` is reset to `"none"` and may remain unset for some failure paths, causing the render-recovery gate to treat those failures as non-recoverable.
  WHY: Any failure path that does not explicitly set the class to lint will be blocked by the gate, even if it is otherwise recoverable.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test file defines a stubbed `classify_preflight_failure` that hardcodes lint results instead of exercising the production classifier.
  WHY: Because the real classifier is never run, regressions in the grep-based classification logic are not covered by these tests.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1189 (within attempt_render_recovery_after_preflight_failure) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The post-rerender call to `classify_preflight_failure` scans the entire accumulated log file, so an earlier failure signature can be matched instead of the actual post-rerender failure.
  WHY: `PRE_FLIGHT_APPEND_LOG="true"` keeps both attempts in the same file, and the classifier’s `grep` patterns can pick the old signature first, producing the wrong recorded reason.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1150-1153 (within attempt_render_recovery_after_preflight_failure) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_CLASS` gate adds a redundant pre-check that can skip recovery based on stale or incorrectly set state.
  WHY: Recovery becomes dependent on a manually maintained variable rather than the classifier, so a future lint-type path that forgets the class assignment would be skipped.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:31-37, 82-86 (and multiple other test cases) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The tests stub out `classify_preflight_failure` with a hardcoded implementation that always returns lint/shell-syntax results.
  WHY: This bypasses the production grep-based classification logic entirely, so real classifier bugs, including log-accumulation misclassification, are not exercised.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1188-1190, 1759-1800 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `classify_preflight_failure` scans the entire `PRE_FLIGHT_LOG_FILE` after rerun, so an older failure pattern may be selected instead of the newest failure.
  WHY: `run_preflight_checks` appends retry output to the existing log, and the `if/elif` grep chain can match an earlier marker first, causing a stale `PRE_FLIGHT_FAILURE_REASON`.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:82-87, 239-244, 376-381, 530-535, 686-691 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test harnesses stub `classify_preflight_failure` with a hard-coded return value instead of invoking the production classifier.
  WHY: This leaves the real classification logic untested in render-recovery scenarios, so regressions such as log misclassification would not be caught.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
